🇺🇦 Syrsky apologized to Fedorov, stating that he does not consider their relationship to be confrontational.

"It was surprising for me to learn that there was a conflict between me and the Minister. I perceived our relationship as professional: with complex issues and different viewpoints. If I offended anyone, Mikhail Albertovich, I apologize. I can be harsh," Syrsky wrote.

According to him, disputes about the army should not be reduced to a confrontation between individuals.

"Ukraine is bigger than Fedorov, Syrsky, and any of us. The war is won by real work, not by public drama surrounding it". 

Syrsky also denied accusations that he is allegedly opposed to the development of drones, stating that he himself initiated the creation of the Unmanned Systems Forces as a separate branch of the military and personally proposed appointing Madyar as their commander. At the same time, he noted that "we need to buy everything, not just what is currently trendy," because the army cannot switch exclusively to drone warfare.

In addition, the Commander-in-Chief criticized the situation with the funding of the army. According to him, after the decision to allocate part of the funds from the salaries of servicemen to the purchase of drones, questions arose regarding payments for the second half of the year. "A soldier's salary is not a reserve for redistribution but an obligation of the state to the people who risk their lives every day," Syrsky said.
